title: Beijing and Moscow present a united front at APEC
text:
Beijing and Moscow present a united front at APEC
Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin both critiqued U.S. leadership in speeches delivered at APEC on Wednesday.
Chinese leader Xi Jinping offered U.S. President Donald Trump a rare gesture of respect and warmth by personally greeting him on the red carpet at Shenzhen Bao’an International Airport on Wednesday.
But Mr. Xi’s hug and smiles came just hours after he and Russian President Vladimir Putin both gave speeches implicitly criticizing the United States, albeit not by name. The comments showed Moscow and Beijing in lockstep ahead of a highly anticipated trilateral meeting with Mr. Trump – and highlighted China’s ongoing effort to promote a more Beijing-centric world order.
“Unliateralism and protectionism are ... rampant,” Mr. Xi stressed in his keynote speech to hundreds of international business leaders gathered in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum. It was a clear reference to U.S. tariffs and export restrictions, which Mr. Xi suggests are contributing to global economic turbulence. In contrast, Mr. Xi cast China as a champion of free trade and shared prosperity, advancing the narrative he’s pushed since Mr. Trump’s return to office: China is the more responsible superpower.
Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are aligned on economic and security issues as they head into talks with U.S. President Donald Trump. One shared goal: to advance a new, multipolar world order.
“China has stood up to unilateralism and protectionism,” he continued, and it “will not waver.”
Mr. Putin made more direct references to the U.S. and other Western nations in his APEC speech, criticizing “former hegemonic powers, acting contrary to the principles of fair competition,” that seek to use “economic coercion” to hold other countries back.
“A fairer, more democratic and more equitable world order is taking shape,” Mr. Putin said, calling this an inevitable shift in the world’s “center of gravity.”
“Old instruments of economic domination ... have largely lost their power to intimidate,” he said, pointing to the failed attempts to isolate Russia as evidence.
Together, the dovetailing remarks by Messrs. Xi and Putin suggested that Mr. Trump would face a unified front in historic trilateral talks between the three leaders scheduled for Thursday. Mr. Xi and Mr. Putin have openly discussed how China and Russia are collaborating to change the U.S.-led world order, to make it better suit their interests.
“China and Russia both believe that a deepened partnership between them is an essential pillar of cultivating more multipolar order,” says Ali Wyne, senior research and advocacy advisor for U.S.-China relations for the International Crisis Group.
Mr. Xi and Mr. Putin have met scores of times since Mr. Xi took power in 2012. The two leaders signed a “no limits” partnership agreement in 2022.
While Mr. Trump seems to have a genuine affinity for Mr. Xi and, to a lesser extent Mr. Putin, their view of him is more opportunistic, experts say. Anticipating that the next U.S. president won’t be as friendly, “they want to extract whatever economic or security concessions they can from Trump during his remaining two years in office,” says Mr. Wyne.
Viewing Mr. Trump as weakened both at home and overseas, they will press for relief from tariffs and economic sanctions. “They want to keep [Trump] onside,” Mr. Wyne says.
In this vein, interactions between the three leaders appeared cordial as they met Wednesday night for an APEC banquet and photo opp. Mr. Xi and Mr. Trump sat together at the dinner, chatting. Mr. Putin approached the U.S. president and shook hands before the photo.
In his APEC speech, Mr. Putin said he saw “substantial” possible benefit from the Nov. 19 trilateral meeting of Russia, China, and the U.S.
“In today’s turbulent world, marked by the fragmentation of the global economy and growing military and political risks, there is an urgent need for unity, not division; equality, not hegemony,” said Mr. Putin, echoing Mr. Xi.
For his part, Mr. Xi presented China as a force for global stability – a word he repeated half a dozen times in his remarks.
“Thanks to the stable environment in our region over the past decades, the Asia-Pacific has ... become an important engine driving global growth,” he said.
He pledged to champion free trade, investment, and unimpeded supply chains, promising that China would offer global businesses “a super-sized open market.”
